findings.statement: The listing described the sets as 'Used - like new. Boxes in good condition.' and the price for the four sets was 200.

Before buying, the buyer specifically asked about box condition and said the box was most of what they were paying for; the seller answered that the sets had been cupboard-stored since new and that 'the boxes are fine'. Box condition was therefore an express term of the bargain, not an incidental detail.

The parcel moved normally through the carrier network and was delivered on 28 August 2026; the buyer reported the damage the same day. Nothing in the tracking record indicates a mishandling event, and nothing in it speaks to condition on arrival.

The buyer's photograph shows one box (LEGO Architecture 21034 London) with a crushed and split upper-left corner and some edge scuffing. The damage is real and visible, but it is localised to one corner: the box is otherwise square, intact, with clean faces and no collapse of the main panels.

Only one of the four boxes is complained of and only one is pictured, so on the current record the shortfall against the description affects roughly a quarter of what was sold, and only the packaging of that quarter rather than its contents.
The seller asserts the box left in good condition and was carefully packed, but has produced no photograph of the sets before dispatch or of the packing method.

provisional.reasoning: The box condition was expressly promised and expressly asked about, so a crushed, split corner on one of the four boxes is a real shortfall against the description. But it is one corner on one box of four, the contents are not said to be affected, and the box is otherwise sound. A refund of about 15% of the price reflects the loss of value on the affected set's packaging while leaving the seller paid for the three undamaged sets and for the parts of the fourth that were as described.

requests.what: A photograph of the outer shipping carton or mailing bag exactly as it arrived, plus the padding/void fill that was inside it, alongside the damaged set.
requests.whyItMatters: The single photo you have supplied shows the damaged corner but nothing about how the parcel travelled. The state of the outer packaging and the amount of protection around the boxes is what distinguishes damage that happened in transit from damage that was already there before dispatch, and that distinction changes how the loss should be borne.

wouldChange.answer: Outer carton shows a matching crush/impact and little or no padding at that corner
wouldChange.implies: Damage occurred in transit through under-protective packing by the seller; seller bears it, but the misdescription was not deliberate

wouldChange.answer: Outer carton is intact and well padded, with no impact where the box corner is crushed
wouldChange.implies: The damage most likely pre-dated dispatch, so the listing and the pre-sale assurance were inaccurate when made

wouldChange.answer: Outer carton shows severe crushing despite generous padding
wouldChange.implies: A carrier mishandling the seller could not reasonably have prevented; the buyer still received less than described but the seller's fault is minimal
Falls back to the general rule that the seller bears the risk of condition on arrival

requests.what: A single photograph showing all four boxes together as received, front and back.
requests.whyItMatters: The complaint and the photo so far concern one box only. The condition of the other three fixes how much of the 200 purchase actually fell short of 'boxes in good condition', which directly sets the size of any refund.

wouldChange.answer: The other three boxes are clean and undamaged
wouldChange.implies: The shortfall is confined to one of four sets

wouldChange.answer: Two or more boxes show comparable crushing or splitting
wouldChange.implies: The 'boxes are fine' assurance fails across most of the purchase

wouldChange.answer: Other boxes show only light shelf wear consistent with 'used - like new'
wouldChange.implies: No additional shortfall beyond the one corner

requests.what: Any photograph of the four boxes taken before or during packing, or any listing photograph of the box that is now damaged, showing that corner.
requests.whyItMatters: You have stated the set was in good condition when it left you. An image of that corner from before dispatch is the most direct way to show the state of the box while it was in your hands, which is the point on which the two accounts differ.

wouldChange.answer: A clear pre-dispatch image shows that corner undamaged
wouldChange.implies: Damage arose after the goods left the seller, in transit

wouldChange.answer: A pre-dispatch or listing image shows the corner already crushed or split
wouldChange.implies: The buyer was assured of a condition the seller could see was untrue
The seller's assertion stands unsupported; the buyer's contemporaneous photo is the only evidence of condition
